name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body:
There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign:
Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: Captain Madison Calder walked her armored destrier down the line of her assembled force, inspecting the condition of their armor and weapons and assessing each soldier for the appropriate level of vigor that would be required for success in the conflict ahead. A dozen Legionnaires perched atop their own warhorses—magnificent creatures, as expertly trained and disciplined as the peerless men and women who would soon ride them into battle. Two Zephyr chariots, one at either end of the row, would protect the flanks of the lancers during their assault, shielding their charge and breaking up enemy formations. At the center of the row of armored cavalry stood four storm-powered warjacks: a pair of Coursers, equipped with grenade launchers and spears and arc node-enabled cortexes that would allow Calder to distribute her arcane abilities to any point on the battlefield, and a pair of Strykers, armed with massive halberds and formidable stormblazer cannons that would electrify the terrain with galvanic fields, deadly to the enemy but that the warcaster's legionnaires would pass harmlessly through in their insulated suits of armor.

name: Name
body: As Calder came to the end of the row, a youthful woman in powered warcaster armor stepped forward, planting the haft of her mechanikal spear in the ground: journeyman warcaster Lieutenant Sarah Brisbane, Calder’s right hand in battle. A third Stryker stood behind her, this one equipped for long-range support with a massive electro-bombard and an optics package that could deliver its devastating shells to any foe they might encounter, even those who might be obfuscated by the dark sorceries of their enemy's spellcaster. "Swift Company is ready for battle, ma’am!" Brisbane announced, loud and proud for the benefit of the entire war host. "Fully charged, in charge, and ready to charge!" In unison, the legionnaires answered Brisbane’s chant with a resounding hurrah while the warjacks clanked with their own mechanikal affirmation. "Indeed, they are, Lieutenant," Calder said, pleased by the polished and ready appearance of her troops. After months of huddling in trenches and sniping from walls as the invaders steadily broke down their defenses and forced the Cygnarans to surrender mile after mile of their beloved homeland, Madison Calder was finally being deployed to do what she had trained her entire military career for.

name: Name
body: Brisbane grinned with satisfaction, dropping the stiff military bravado. "Madison, if I didn’t know better, I’d say you had conquest on the mind." "You know what they say about the best defense…" Calder said, pivoting her horse and taking her position at the front of the lancers. "You’ll never see it coming," Brisbane finished one of Calder’s many well-known maxims. Calder looked skyward. A few tufts of clouds were all that was visible in the otherwise electric-blue morning sky. "Looks like a storm’s brewing," she called out. Behind her, the legionnaires answered with a round of eager cheers. Raising her sword overhead, she spurred the sides of her mount. "Today, we take back what’s ours!" Her powerful grey warhorse broke into a gallop. And thunder followed.

name: Name
body: Night is the great equalizer in wartime. The cloak of darkness emboldens the weak and makes mighty the small, transforming even a single warrior into a saboteur or assassin that can wreak havoc upon an entire army. And for even the greatest army, the veil of night exposes every vulnerability while blinding them to the dangers unseen. Night is a time to endure or a time to exploit, favoring those without the means to face their enemies fairly and condemning those who have underestimated the consequences of their actions in the light.

name: Name
body:
This scenario reflects a clandestine operation in which the Defenders are attempting to sneak into the Invaders’ camp and burn their transport vessels moored along the river, effectively cutting the Invaders off from their main force. The Invaders have struck deeply into Defender territory and are now overextended. If the Defenders can cut off these overextended elements from the main force, the Invaders will be unable to reinforce their position during the main offensive and will be easier to eliminate as they are forced to make their way back to enemy-held territory over land.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender has 50 points to build their army.
The Invader has 75 points to build their army.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, a river runs along 8" of the left side of the table. The Invader’s Deployment Zone runs another 8" along it. The Invader places four 3"×5" Transport Vessel objectives lengthwise anywhere in contact with the shoreline/left edge of the Invader’s Deployment Zone.
The river and the Transport Vessel objectives are impassable terrain.
The Invader then places four 4"×4" obstructions representing tents anywhere in their Deployment Zone.
Finally, the Invader can place up to five additional terrain features anywhere on the table. The Defender can then place up to two terrain features anywhere outside the river or the Invader’s Deployment Zone. A player cannot place a terrain feature within 4" of a Transport Vessel objective, a tent, or another terrain feature.
The Defender cannot place defenses in this scenario.
The Defender does not deploy their models in this scenario. Instead, before deployment, the Defender divides their forces into two to four Raiding Teams. The Defender records which of their models/units are in each Raiding Team. In addition to their actual Raiding Teams, the Defender begins with two Decoys. Raiding Teams and Decoys are represented by 30 mm markers on the table. The bottom of each marker should be noted with either the Raiding Team it corresponds to or that it is a Decoy.

name: Name
body:
After the Invader has deployed, the Defender places their Raiding Team markers and Decoys in contact with the edge of the table opposite the Invader’s Deployment Zone.
During each of their Maintenance Phases, the Defender can place each Raiding Team marker and Decoy anywhere within 12" of its current location. After their first turn, instead of placing a Raiding Team marker, the Defender can choose to reveal it. When a Raiding Team marker is revealed, the Defender places the models/units in the Raiding Team anywhere completely within 6" of the marker. These models can activate normally that turn.
If an Invader model that ends its movement or is placed within 6" of a Raiding Team marker or Decoy and has line of sight to it, the marker or Decoy must be revealed. If a Decoy is revealed, remove it from the table. If a Raiding Team is revealed, the Defender must immediately place the models in the Raiding Team anywhere completely within 4" of the marker.
Revealed Leader models and Horrors are put into play with their starting focus, fury, or essence points.

name: Name
body: Note that Raiding Team markers and Decoys are not models and cannot be targeted. Because the Defender is placing Raiding Team markers and Decoys at the start of the game, their models lose Advance Deploy and Ambush.

name: Name
body:
A Defender model that begins its activation in base contact with a Transport Vessel objective can make a special action to set fire to it. The Defender gains 2 Victory Points each time a Transport Vessel objective is set on fire. Each objective can be set on fire only once.
The Invader gains 1 Victory Point each time their models reveal a Raiding Team marker or Decoy. The Invader gains 2 additional Victory Points if their models reveal the Raiding Team that the Defender’s Leader model is a part of.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If at any time all four Transport Vessel objectives are on fire, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points. If at the end of the sixth round, two or fewer Transport Vessel objectives are on fire, the Invader wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Conquest is a precarious endeavor. With each battle won, territory once secured is made vulnerable. Through success, the conqueror’s resources are stretched thinner across a greater area, and like a rope pulled too far, it can eventually snap. But desperate for a reprieve, the clever foe can accelerate the inevitable, severing supply lines and cutting off the conqueror’s operational nodes. Without the connective lines of communication and supplies, the fragile structure of the conquest will crumble.

name: Name
body:
As the Defender offensive grinds on, the Invaders begin to feel the heat. In this scenario, a desperate group of Invaders attempts to cross enemy territory to warn their generals of the impending Defender main attack. Even if they cannot escape their fates, the Invaders may yet warn their forces by igniting enough signal fires at the edge of their camp as they cross the battlefield.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender has 75 points to build their army.
The Invader has 50 points to build their army.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, the Invader deploys to a 12"×12" area in the middle of a table edge. The Defender has two 8" Deployment Zones running along the table edges to the right and left of the Invader’s Deployment Zone.
Place a 30 mm Signal Fire objective centered 24" from the rear edge of the Invader’s Deployment Zone and 14" from the right table edge. Place a second 30 mm Signal Fire objective centered 24" from the rear edge of the Invader’s Deployment Zone and 14" from the left table edge. Place a third 30 mm Signal Fire objective centered 14" from the table edge opposite the Invader’s Deployment Zone and 24" from the right and left table edges.
Players then alternate placing terrain features with each player placing up to four features. A player cannot place terrain within 4" of an objective, Deployment Zone, table edge, or another terrain feature.
The Defender cannot place defenses in this scenario.
The Defender deploys their models first and the Invader takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
An Invader model in base contact with a Signal Fire objective can make a special action to ignite the signal fire. The Invader gains 2 Victory Points each time a Signal Fire objective is lit.
A Defender model in base contact with a Signal Fire objective that is on fire can make a special action to put the fire out. The Defender gains a Victory Point each time a Signal Fire objective is put out.
The Defender gains 1 Victory Point each time an Invader solo or unit is destroyed or removed from play.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If the Invader can move a warrior model off the opposite table edge they deployed to (marked on the map as the Escape Edge), the Invader wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points. If the Invader has not won after six rounds and no Signal Fire objectives are lit, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Invaders will predictably underestimate the value of the holdings they capture. What they see as a resource-providing asset or a strategically located access point may hold much greater importance to those they have taken it from. And this unknown worth can be motivating beyond any rationale, driving the displaced to risk tremendously in the liberation of something the conqueror is unready to pay so dearly for.

name: Name
body:
After months of training, reconnaissance, and operations intended to wear down the enemy’s defenses, the Defenders are finally ready to launch their main offensive against the Invaders. The Invaders hold a strategically important industrial village, and the Defenders have vowed to drive them out once and for all.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
The Invader deploys within 10" of the north table edge. The Defender deploys within 7" of the south table edge.
Place a 4"×8" Command Tent objective in the middle of the Invader’s Deployment Zone so that it touches the forward edge of the zone as shown on the map. The Command Tent is an obstruction.
The Defender and Invader then take turns placing the following Building objectives:
Alchemist’s Shop: This objective is an obstruction that must be at least 6"×8". While you are securing the Alchemist’s Shop, the ranged weapons of friendly models within 5" of the objective gain +2 RNG.
Granary: This objective is an obstruction that must be at least 6"×8". If you are securing the Granary objective during your Maintenance Phase, you can remove d3+1 damage points from a friendly living model anywhere on the table.
Park: This objective is a 6" diameter area of open terrain. While you hold the Park, friendly models/units in the Park cannot be targeted by enemy spells.
Repair Shop: This objective is an obstruction that must be at least 6"×8". If you are  securing the Repair Shop objective during your Maintenance Phase, you can remove d3+1 damage points from a friendly construct model anywhere on the table.

name: Name
body:
A Building objective cannot be placed within 5" of a Deployment Zone or another Building objective.
Players then alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to two features. A player cannot place terrain within 4" of an objective, Deployment Zone, or another terrain feature.
The Defender cannot place defenses in this scenario.
The Invader sets up first and the Defender takes the first turn.

name: Name
body: High Alert: If the Invader won the Running the Gauntlet scenario, the Defender’s models lose Advance Deployment and Ambush in this scenario. Reinforcements: The Invader can call in reinforcements during the game. If the Invader won the Night Raid scenario, they can call for reinforcements twice during the game. If the Defender won the Night Raid scenario, the Invader can call for reinforcements once during the game. The Invader can call for reinforcements at the end of any of their turns. When they do so, return one destroyed solo or unit to play, placing it anywhere completely within 5" of the Command Tent. Gobber Spy Mission: Players who include Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, in their force can undertake the following covert missions: Defender: Gather Intel—Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, can make the Gather Intel special action once per game while in base contact with the Command Tent objective. When he does so, the Defender receives 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body: Invader: Rear Guard—Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, can make a Rear Guard special action once per game while in the Defender’s Deployment Zone. When he does so, the Invader receives 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body: Starting on the second round, at the beginning of each of their turns, a player scores 1 Victory Point for each Building objective they are holding or securing.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: At the beginning of any of their turns beginning with the third, if a player is securing all four Building objectives, they win the match and receive 6 War Chest points. Additionally, if the Defender player begins a turn securing the Command Tent objective, they win the match and receive 6 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
